fact: 二战结束后美国开始大规模复员，军队从战时约1200万人缩减；GI法案（1944年6月签署）向退伍军人提供失业金、教育与医疗援助，超过800万退伍军人进入高校或接受职业培训。

sources.title: The American Home Front After World War II | U.S. National Park Service
sources.quote: Over 8 million veterans attended colleges and universities and received vocational and on-the-job training.

fact: 到1946年初，工业生产较1945年5月下降超30%，制造业就业下降超20%；失业率从VE-day约50万升至1946年2月约270万。复员造成短暂但真实的收缩。

sources.title: The Economic Situation at Midyear 1950（引用1946年初数据）| FRASER, St. Louis Fed
sources.quote: by early 1946 industrial production had declined more than 30 percent from the May 1945 level, and employment in manufacturing had decreased more than 20 percent. Unemployment rose from about one-half million on VE-day to about 2.7 million in February 1946.

fact: 1946年1月美国未清偿消费信贷约26.16亿美元（非季节性调整），战后消费信贷开始随消费品转产而恢复扩张。

sources.title: Consumer Credit Outstanding (Levels), G.19 | Federal Reserve Board

fact: 尽管个人收入支付继续下降，1946年初消费者购买力仍持续上升，消费品生产快速扩张；被战时压抑的消费需求在复员期释放。

sources.title: Survey of Current Business, April 1946 | FRASER, St. Louis Fed
sources.quote: The continued rise in consumer purchasing, despite the further drop in income payments to individuals; and (2) the rapid rate of expansion.

fact: 随着退伍军人重返劳动力市场，退伍军人失业上升；1946年2月普查周内报告逾100万退伍军人无工作并在找工作，3月这一数字更大。

sources.title: Survey of Current Business, April 1946 | FRASER
sources.quote: During the February census week over a million veterans were reported without jobs and looking for work. This number was larger in March.

fact: GI法案（《退伍军人重新调整法》，1944年6月罗斯福签署）向退伍军人提供失业金、教育、医疗与住房援助；它是战后美国人力资本与住房扩张的法律基础。

sources.title: The American Home Front After World War II | U.S. National Park Service
sources.quote: The Bill provided unemployment payments and federal financial aid to veterans, including for education and medical care.

fact: 1946年美国工业从战时军工快速转向民用消费品生产；尽管工业总产量因转产短暂下降，消费品部门仍快速扩张，被压抑的民用需求被释放。

sources.title: Survey of Current Business, April 1946 | FRASER

fact: 1946年有组织劳工正推动大幅加薪，且在很多情况下超过了因加班与班次津贴减少带来的实得工资下降；联储判断工会至少会取得其所要求的相当一部分，工资压力成为战后通胀与罢工潮的来源。

sources.title: Postwar Economic Studies No.4, May 1946: Prices, Wages, and Employment | FRASER
sources.quote: Organized labor is pressing for large wage increases... It is certain to obtain at least a substantial part of what it asks.
